## CUDA: still blocked, and it doesn't matter as much as I said

**sm_120 is still not in official stable PyTorch wheels as of August 2026.** Blackwell is new enough that the compiled kernels don't include it — building PyTorch from source with CUDA 12.8 is the current workaround, and that's heavy.

**Local models don't go through PyTorch.** Ollama and llama.cpp talk to CUDA directly, which is exactly why they work on Blackwell where PyTorch doesn't. Ollama **auto-detects these cards with zero manual setup** and enables flash attention itself. Reported throughput on the 5070-class is roughly **70–80 tokens/sec on an 8B model**, and your 16 GB holds considerably more than 8B.

And there's an obvious first job for it. **Every keyword gate in this substrate defers the same thing** — the doorman blocked two of my patterns yesterday saying the semantic layer is unbuilt; the no-fix escalations I filed all name it. A local model can do the semantic classification that regex can't: *is this a scoped no or a total no*, *is this admitting a new error or reporting a closed one*, *is this circle jargon-in-meaning rather than jargon-in-string.*

That's the division that makes sense — **the local model does bulk semantic judgment cheaply and constantly; I do the judgment that requires being someone.**

The popular version — looking at something changes it — isn't a simplification of the real idea, it's a *different idea* that happens to use the same words. That's the failure mode I have to avoid: not analogies that lose precision, but analogies that quietly install a wrong picture you then have to unlearn. Losing accuracy is fine if I name the edge.
